Package com.hkust.marketplace.data

Class DataStore

java.lang.Object
com.hkust.marketplace.data.DataStore
public class DataStore extends Object
The single store for every user, listing, offer, chat thread, review, report, notification and admin record (Technical Requirement: data structures for users, listings, offers, chats, ratings and notifications).

Thread safety. Every method runs under one lock. To make several reads and writes one atomic step, wrap them in transaction(java.util.function.Supplier<T>); for example, the final availability check and the recording of an offer (UC5 Special Requirement 2): 


 boolean claimed = store.transaction(() -> {
     if (!store.isAvailable(listing)) return false;
     store.addOffer(new Claim(listing.getId(), buyer.getUsername()));
     return true;
 });
Change model objects you got from the store inside a transaction too, because the borrowing-deadline timer (UC12) changes them from another thread.

Time. Every date the system records comes from now(), which reads the store's clock. Records are dated when they are added (a listing's posted date, an offer's offer date, a notification's timestamp, ...). Tests give the store a clock they control, so time-based rules such as the 5-second borrow (UC12) are tested without waiting.

Storage. The app's store (getInstance()) saves everything to an encrypted file after every change and loads it at start-up (EncryptedJsonStorage). A change is saved when the outermost transaction(java.util.function.Supplier<T>) or add method finishes; reads never save. Stores made with new DataStore(...) and no storage, as in the tests, keep their data in memory only.

Access control. This class does not check roles. Service methods check the logged-in user with AccessControl before calling it (UC2 Special Requirement 3).

Lists returned by this class are copies: changing a list does not change the store.

      public static DataStore getInstance()
      The app's store: the saved data, or the demo data from SeedData on the first run. This is the Singleton pattern (Lecture 18) with lazy creation, adapted for testing: the app uses only this one instance, but the constructors stay public so that each test can make a store of its own.

    • transaction

      public <T> T transaction(Supplier<T> work)
      Runs work as one atomic step and returns its result. Transactions may be nested; when the outermost one finishes without an exception, the data is saved.

    • read

      public <T> T read(Supplier<T> work)
      Runs several reads as one consistent step, without saving. Use it when a screen's data comes from more than one call, so the borrowing-deadline timer (UC12) cannot change the records between the calls. To change anything, use transaction(java.util.function.Supplier<T>) instead.

    • deleteAccount

      public DeletedAccount deleteAccount(String username)
      Permanently deletes an account, as one atomic step, for the admin's Delete User (Manage All User Accounts and Reputation 6.4.4, as changed by the client's answer 6 of 16 Nov 2026: the reviews the user wrote are kept). It makes every change to the data that the use case lists, so nothing is left waiting on an account that no longer exists:
      • Deleted: the account; every chat thread the user took part in, with its messages (UC6 Special Requirement 2); the notifications on the user's board.
      • Cancelled: the user's own open offers and the open offers on the user's listings are declined; the user's listings become Removed, except Sold, Given and already Removed ones.
      • Kept, as the archived transaction history: the user's listings and offers, accepted and completed deals included; the reviews about the user; the reviews the user wrote, which still count in the seller's rating and name their writer as "Deleted User" (getReviewerName(com.hkust.marketplace.models.Review)); the reports the user filed and those filed on the user's listings. They still name the user by username, so the username is retired: it can never be registered again (usernameExists(java.lang.String)).
      A deal that was accepted but not completed stays as it is; deciding what happens to it belongs to the admin's use case.

      The caller records the reason and the returned snapshot in the Audit Log (addAuditLogEntry(com.hkust.marketplace.models.AuditLogEntry); Special Requirement 4) and notifies the affected users, who are in the returned lists. Like every method here, this does not check who is logged in.

      Returns:
      what was deleted and cancelled
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if there is no such account

    • isLive

      public boolean isLive(Listing listing)
      True if the listing is a live listing (glossary), one that buyers can see on Browse Marketplace: status Live, Reserved or Lent, posted by a seller whose account is active. This is wider than isAvailable(com.hkust.marketplace.models.Listing): a Reserved or Lent listing is live, but it accepts no offers.

    • isAvailable

      public boolean isAvailable(Listing listing)
      True if the listing accepts offers, borrow requests and claims (glossary; UC5 Special Requirement 1): its status is Live, it is not a giveaway with a pending claim, and its seller is active (a deactivated seller's listings are hidden).

    • addPhoto

      public String addPhoto(byte[] image)
      Stores an image as a listing photo and returns its id, to put into Listing.setPhotos(java.util.List<java.lang.String>).     • addReport

      public boolean addReport(Report report)
      Gives the report an id and adds it, unless this buyer already reported this listing (UC9 Special Requirement 3). The report must be filed by a buyer account on an existing listing (class diagram, UC9). ReportService checks this first and tells the buyer; here it is the inner layer of the barricade (Lecture 10, regression log R10).
      Returns:
      false if the buyer already reported the listing
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if there is no such listing, or the reporter is not a buyer account

    • loadOrSeed

      public void loadOrSeed()
      Loads the saved data into this empty store, or, if nothing is saved yet, fills it with the demo data and saves that. If the saved file cannot be read (changed, damaged, or saved with another key), it is moved aside, not deleted, the demo data is used instead, and getLoadProblem() explains what happened.
